question: Rhinocerebral mucormycosis is caused by fungi that produce broad, septate hyphae branching at acute 45-degree angles.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Mucor species produce wide ASEPTATE hyphae branching at RIGHT ANGLES (90°). Septate hyphae with acute-angle (45°) branching describe Aspergillus, not Mucor. Confusing the two leads to incorrect antifungal choice — mucormycosis requires amphotericin B (not voriconazole, which covers Aspergillus).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. Mucor species produce wide ASEPTATE (pauci-septate) hyphae that branch at RIGHT ANGLES (90°). The description of narrow septate hyphae with acute-angle (45°) dichotomous branching is characteristic of Aspergillus. This morphological distinction on tissue biopsy is diagnostically critical.
